content: Your doctor has prescribed torsemide to help reduce the amount of excess fluid in your body. This medication will either be added to an intravenous fluid that is administered through a needle or catheter placed in your vein, or it may be injected directly into your vein or catheter over a period of at least two minutes. In some cases, torsemide may be prescribed for other purposes; if you have questions about this, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Your healthcare provider will monitor the effectiveness of the treatment and check for side effects through laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is essential to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your body responds to the medication. Before starting torsemide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to torsemide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Let your doctor know if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney or liver problems. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while taking torsemide. If you become pregnant during treatment, contact your doctor immediately. Before administering torsemide, carefully inspect the solution. It should be clear and free of any floating particles. Check the bag or container for leaks by gently squeezing it or observing it closely. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Instead, use a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is crucial to follow your healthcare provider’s instructions exactly when using this medication. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your provider. If you encounter a mechanical issue, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, your healthcare provider may advise you to stop the infusion. Torsemide may cause side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: frequent urination, muscle cramps, weakness, dizziness, faintness, fatigue, headache, confusion, thirst, upset stomach, or vomiting. In rare cases, torsemide can cause serious side effects. If you experience rapid and excessive weight loss or vomit blood, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Your healthcare provider may supply you with several days’ worth of torsemide at a time. Store the medication as directed by your provider. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and always store medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will also instruct you on how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If you are receiving torsemide through a vein or under the skin, be aware of the signs of a catheter-related infection. Notify your healthcare provider immediately if you notice tenderness, warmth, irritation, drainage, redness, swelling, or pain near the site where the needle enters your vein or skin. Torsemide is also sold under the brand name Demadex®.
